question_bank.stem: A pretrained language model can continue internet text well but still be unhelpful to users because pretraining teaches it to do what?

options.text: Rank multiple answers by human preference
Estimate rewards for full generated answers
Continue text rather than answer questions

question_bank.rationale: The gap is that next-token pretraining produces text continuation ability, not direct helpful question answering.

distractor_rationales.A: Preference ranking is part of reward-model data collection, not pretraining.
distractor_rationales.B: Reward estimation is added later in RLHF.
distractor_rationales.C: Epsilon-greedy is a DQN exploration method, not LM pretraining.

source_ref.evidence_span: was trained to continue text rather than answer questions.

frame_evidence.description: Language-model training recap slide shows a training objective with input text, model parameters, output next word, loss, and gradient.

question_bank.stem: Supervised fine-tuning for helpfulness trains the pretrained model on what kind of data?

options.text: Random state-action transitions from Atari games
Pairwise reward margins from a scalar critic
Unlabeled web text with next-token prediction only

question_bank.rationale: SFT collects prompts and human-written responses, then fine-tunes the pretrained model to imitate those demonstrations.

distractor_rationales.A: Atari transitions are for DQN, not LLM SFT.
distractor_rationales.C: Pairwise reward margins are part of reward-model/RLHF training.
distractor_rationales.D: That describes pretraining rather than supervised fine-tuning.

frame_evidence.description: SFT slide shows a pretrained model fine-tuned on a human-written prompt and response demonstration.

question_bank.stem: The lecture identifies SFT's limitation as imitation rather than direct optimization of what signal?
question_bank.rationale: SFT teaches the model to imitate good human-written behavior, while RLHF is introduced to optimize preferences more directly.

distractor_rationales.B: Pixel velocity belongs to Breakout frame stacking.
distractor_rationales.C: Discount factors are part of RL returns, not the SFT limitation.
distractor_rationales.D: Terminal flags are DQN implementation details.

frame_evidence.description: SFT slide shows a pretrained model fine-tuned on a human-written prompt and response demonstration.

question_bank.stem: The transition from SFT toward RLHF is motivated by moving beyond human-written demonstrations toward what training target?

options.text: A larger Q-table for language tokens
A terminal-state Boolean for each prompt
A cropped grayscale view of the input text

question_bank.rationale: The lecture calls preference the key word and sets up RLHF as the next step beyond SFT imitation.

distractor_rationales.A: Language-model alignment is not framed as a token Q-table here.
distractor_rationales.B: Terminal booleans are DQN mechanics, not the SFT-to-RLHF target.
distractor_rationales.D: Cropping and grayscale are Atari preprocessing steps.

source_ref.evidence_span: And the word preference is the keyword.
